subject: FinPay discovery \u000B competitive TCO follow-ups and next tests
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@finpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: FinPay discovery � competitive TCO follow-ups and next tests

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we can validate performance and unit economics against your current vendor and the hyperscalers:  

Summary of what we heard
- Primary goal: 1) reduce per-call inference spend on high-volume async pipelines, 2) meet p95 latency targets for interactive flows (<=200ms) for the agent UI.
- Current pain: high egress + per-request overhead with your current provider; inconsistent cache hit rates when you move to multi-tenant endpoints.
- Important constraints: PCI-adjacent data, want VPC/private deployment option for production.

How Redwood differentiates (short)
- Cost controls: intelligent batching + prefix/KV caching to reduce token counts and effective per-1M token cost.
- Predictable reserved capacity (Dedicated) for sustained throughput and predictable p95 latencies.
- Smart routing + model variants: automated fallback to lower-cost model slices for non-critical workloads.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown so you can measure unit economics per route.

Proposed tests to validate claims (we recommend running both):
1) Latency / throughput run (interactive agent path)
   - Model: Mistral-Chat-8B (quantized run)
   - Targets: batch size 1-8 for interactive, p95 <= 200ms at target QPS of 40
   - Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, and per-1M-token cost (including batching overhead)

2) Bulk async TCO run (high-throughput pipelines)
   - Model: Llama-2-13B variant with KV caching enabled
   - Targets: sustained QPS to generate 1M tokens in < 6 hours; measure cache hit rate (goal >= 35-40%) and per-1M tokens cost with/without cache
   - Metrics: average tokens/sec, batch sizes used, cache hit %, and resulting unit cost per 1M tokens

Initial ballpark unit economics (hosted API, public pricing estimate for comparison):
- Redwood hosted (baseline joint estimate): ~$7.50 per 1M tokens (no caching; single-request processing)
- With batching + caching applied in a realistic workload: effective cost can drop to ~$2.50	6$4.00 per 1M tokens depending on cache hit rate and batching profile
- Hyperscaler example (public reference): ~ $12	6$18 per 1M tokens for comparable managed endpoints depending on SLA and egress assumptions

What we need from you to set up tests
- A small representative request corpus for both interactive and async workloads (or example prompts + typical length distribution).
- Preferred test window (we can run overnight).
- Any constraints on IP/payload or data residency for Private/Dedicated runs.

Next steps / mutual action plan
- You: share the sample corpus and confirm the test window by EOD Thursday (Aug 20).
- Redwood: provision a test harness, run the two tests, and deliver a short report with p95 latency, cache hit rate, and per-1M token cost.
- If Dedicated is desired, we'll include a dedicated capacity quote with projected per-1M token unit economics and SLA.

I've attached an initial TCO workbook and our benchmark summary (PDF) to make the calculations explicit. Let me know if you want us to include a side-by-side dedicated vs hosted forecast in the workbook.

Thanks  happy to hop on a quick 30m next week to review results.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: finpay-initial-tco.xlsx, redwood-benchmarks.pdf

From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@finpay.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Lopez <t.lopez@finpay.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinPay discovery � competitive TCO follow-ups and next tests

Thanks, Aditya  this is exactly the kind of detail we need. A couple quick clarifications before we share the corpus:  

1) Can you include a Dedicated (reserved capacity) estimate that shows: committed monthly price, projected per-1M token payment when fully utilized (assume 60% utilization) and the SLA for p95? We want to compare reserved vs hosted.
2) For the hosted numbers above, can you show line items that separate model compute costs vs network/egress and request overhead? Our procurement team needs that level of granularity for total cost ownership.
3) For the cache hit rate examples you cited (35-40%), what workload assumptions drive that number? Is that prefix-only caching or KV cache for multi-turn?

We can share a sanitized request corpus  I will confirm with Tom and send it by Thursday morning. If you could also flag any privacy/residency limitations we need to be aware of for the Private deployment option, that would help.

Appreciate it  Sarah
Sarah Kim
Sr. Product Manager, FinPay
sarah.kim@finpay.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: FinPay discovery � test config notes

Forwarding Sarah's clarifying questions. Quick internal notes for test engineering:  

- For Dedicated quote: prepare two profiles  (A) 99% workload reserve for production agent (target p95 <= 200ms) and (B) mixed batch + async pool for nightly high-throughput jobs. Provide estimated monthly commit and break down into effective $/1M tokens at 60% and 90% utilization.
- For the hosting breakdown Sarah wants: split compute (GPU hours), network/egress, and orchestration/request overhead. Use conservative egress assumptions (FinPay expects significant outbound usage).
- Cache assumptions: run both prefix-only and KV cache multi-turn tests. For KV cache, target 40% cache hit in the async run by tuning TTLs and cache keys; capture hit distribution across request types.

I'll scope a 1-day harness: run 1M-token-run for both models listed by Aditya, and collect p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, batching distribution, cache-hit per-key. Laura  can you take the lead on setting up the quantized Mistral run? I can quote from infra for Dedicated once I have utilization profiles.

-Marcus
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@finpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinPay discovery � competitive TCO follow-ups and next tests

Thanks Sarah  great questions. We're aligned on actions:  

- I'll have the TCO workbook updated with a Dedicated vs Hosted comparison and a line-item breakout (compute / network / request overhead) and upload by end of day Friday.
- Marcus and Laura are standing up the test harness; proposed test window is Saturday 08/22 02:00 - 08:00 PT (overnight)  please confirm if that works for you.

- For cache assumptions: the 35-40% range is an initial expectation for the async pipeline with KV caching turned on and tuned TTLs; we'll report the observed rate and include sensitivity analysis in the results.

Attached: updated finpay-initial-tco.xlsx (tabbed: Hosted-Baseline, Dedicated-Projections, Cost-Breakdown)

If the Saturday window looks good, we'll proceed and share the report + recommended next steps (including a Dedicated commitment proposal if results meet your targets).

Best,
Aditya

Attachments: finpay-initial-tco.xlsx (updated)
